text: Corpus access and the window bag, for the adopted CoAtNet arm.

The corpus is published preprocessed (dreaddevelopment/knee-raptor-corpus plus -ext, CC0-1.0): two uint8 arrays of shape (N, 44, 336, 336) that together hold 4,407 studies, with a companion (N, 44) mask marking which slices are real. Nothing here decodes a DICOM.
A study becomes a bag of windows, not a stack of slices.
Each window is three physically consecutive slices stacked as the three channels of one RGB image -- most of the benefit of a 3D model at the cost of a 2D one.
Training draws k window centres at random every epoch, so the same study presents differently each time;
the resampling is the augmentation, and apart from a mild intensity jitter nothing else is augmented.
No flips: laterality is signal here, not nuisance (Medial/Lateral are separate findings).
Two contracts this module exists to enforce, because breaking either is silent:
Row order. Part 1 precedes part 2 in the volumes, the masks and the ids alike.
Sorting any one of them independently mis-pairs studies with images and the run still trains, just on scrambled supervision.
The teacher is llm_labels_raw.csv, never llm_labels.csv. The latter carries gold values in its 58 is_gold rows, so a model trained on it scores gold 1.0000 and means nothing.
Those same 58 rows are the right source of validation truth -- the trap is using them to train.
The normalisation the adopted inference notebook applies to every window (eval_windows, cell 47): x = (x - _MEAN) / _STD with the ImageNet constants, under NORM = "imagenet".
This module divided by 255 and stopped, which is a real mismatch and not a stylistic one: measured 2026-09-18, their inputs carry ~4.48x our standard deviation and a -0.24 mean shift.
A model trained on [0, 1] and scored on that is being shown a different distribution, and -- worse -- the kernel runs clean and the low score reads as "our arm is worse" rather than as a bug.
imagenet is also what sw_in12k_ft_in1k was pretrained under, so it is the distribution the frozen features expect.
The default stays none so the 2026-09-18 fold remains exactly reproducible;
choosing imagenet is an explicit, pre-registered change.
The two corpus parts as one (N, D, H, W) read-only view.
Never concatenated on disk: 22 GB of copying to serve reads that are always a single study.
Indexing is by global row, part 1 first.
Memory-map both parts.
Refuses a half-staged corpus.

The single-file fallback that other ports carry is deliberately absent: with only part 1 present a run trains on 3,200 of the 4,407 studies and reports nothing wrong, because part 2 holds the other 1,207.

Teacher targets for training, gold truth for scoring.
Returns (train_ids, gold_ids, targets) where targets maps every uid in either list to a float32 vector of 12.
A gold study is never given teacher targets -- it carries its expert values whether or not it trains.
train_gold is the 2026-09-20 operator ruling, "testing and validation will be done on the submission kernel, no holding out anything".
With it on, the 58 gold studies join train_ids carrying their GOLD vectors, and the 58 stop being a ruler.

The measured reason (T115/T117): gold-58 could not separate any two of our three CoAtNet recipes -- paired deltas +0.0036 / +0.0079 / +0.0043 against bands +/-0.020 to +/-0.028 -- while selecting on it added +0.004 to +0.013 of upward bias to the number then read.
It was doing two jobs badly and its best use is as the only 58 rows of truth in the corpus.
gold_ids is returned either way, because the gold set is still SCORED -- as a floor that refuses below 0.85, never as a selector.
See T117 rule 3.
The gold rows get their EXPERT values in both modes.
The only thing train_gold changes is whether the optimizer ever sees them;
it never changes what they say.
A gold study given teacher targets would be the worst of both -- trained on, and on the wrong labels.
Score the TEACHER file itself against gold-58, in process.
This is the one check that distinguishes the teacher from its decoys.
llm_labels_raw.csv reads 0.8976 here -- the documented teacher, the best of seven public label sets.
llm_labels.csv, llm_labels_recal.csv, weak_labels.csv and weak_labels_distilled.csv all read 1.0000, because their 58 is_gold rows carry the gold values rather than a model's output.

A run supervised by one of those is not wrong at train time -- the gold studies are held out either way -- but every claim made about "what our teacher is worth" would be measuring gold against itself.
An earlier version of this guard tested the training rows for saturation and passed on a leaked file, because the leak is in rows training never sees.
A check that cannot fail on the thing it names is worse than none.
Two guards, and only one of them is conditional.
THE SPLIT ASSERTION is about accident: gold in the training set when nobody asked for it.
Under the 2026-09-20 ruling gold in training is the point, so the assertion is gated on the flag rather than deleted -- with the flag off it still fires, which is what keeps the old mode honest.
THE TEACHER-FILE CEILING IS NOT CONDITIONAL, and must never become so.

It scores the LABEL FILE against gold, not the model, so train_gold cannot make a high reading legitimate: data/llm_labels.csv carries the gold values in its 58 is_gold rows and reads 1.0000, where llm_labels_raw.csv -- the teacher -- reads 0.8976.
Passing the first where the second belongs trains every study on labels derived from the evaluation set, and this line is the only thing between us and that.
REFUSING TO TRAIN: train_gold is on but the gold studies are not all in the training split.
Under the 2026-09-20 ruling nothing is held out;
a partial split is neither mode and would be silently reported as either.

That is a file whose gold rows carry gold values, not a teacher.
The teacher is built from data/llm_labels_raw.csv and reads ~0.8976.
THE TYPED SLOT LAYOUTS the corpus may be packed with, and the reason a triplet has to be constrained at all.

The adopted notebook defines two: _SLOTS44 = [("Sagittal", 1, 12), ("Sagittal", 0, 10), ("Coronal", 1, 8), ("Coronal", 0, 6), ("Axial", -1, 8)] _SLOTS64 = [("Sagittal", 1, 18), ("Sagittal", 0, 14), ("Coronal", 1, 12), ("Coronal", 0, 8), ("Axial", -1, 12)] packed SEQUENTIALLY, so the (plane, sequence) boundaries of the 44-slot packing fall at 12, 22, 30, 36.
A window centred on one of those stacks three channels drawn from two different planes.
[lo, hi) per typed group for depth, or ONE group when the packing is unknown.
Returned rather than hardcoded in two places: the constraint and the checks that pin it must read the SAME table, or a check passes while the trainer uses different boundaries.
AN UNKNOWN DEPTH IS NOT AN ERROR, AND IS NOT A SILENT FALLBACK EITHER.
The constraint makes two guarantees -- a triplet stays inside one typed group, and it touches no blank slot.
A corpus that is not one of the notebook's two packings has no typed groups, so the first guarantee is VACUOUS rather than violated, and the second still holds in full.
The smoke suite's stub corpus (depth 8) is exactly that case.
Returning one group is therefore honest: it says "no boundaries here", not "never mind the boundaries".
One study -> (K, 3, res, res) float32 in [0,1], plus its 12 targets.
set in _ensure, from the opened corpus

THE DEFECT THIS REPLACES (T119).
This read
lo, hi = int(valid.min()), int(valid.max()) cs = list(range(lo + 1, hi))
-- the outer ends of the whole valid span, and nothing else.

The corpus packs 44 TYPED slots sequentially (SLOT_GROUPS), so a centre at slot 22 produced a triplet whose three channels were sagittal, coronal, coronal: a "2.5D adjacent" stack of three different anatomical planes.

Measured over all 3,200 corpus rows with the real masks: 19.0% of the eval draw and 16.7% of the training draw spanned a group boundary, and 5.7% / 5.0% touched a blank slot -- range(lo+1, hi) never looked at the interior, so blanks inside the span were legal centres.
The adopted notebook's own _eval_centers has the same two holes, so this is INHERITED and is NOT the cause of the -0.010 T118 measured against their checkpoint -- both sides ate it.

Viability was measured before this was written: clean centres per study are mean 32.8, median 34, min 22 against a theoretical 34, so no study is starved and the training k=12 never repeats for want of choices.

k_eval=42 exceeds the 34 that exist, so the eval draw repeats ~8 of them -- deliberate, and registered in T119 rule 1: legality is the variable under test and the window COUNT is held fixed, because k_eval is part of the decode key.
clean is an argument rather than only an attribute because getitem must be able to say "this particular study cannot be drawn cleanly" without lying to this method about the corpus (T120 finding 2).
None means "use the fold's rule", which is every ordinary call.

T120 FINDING 2 -- THE SYNTHETIC VALIDITY SET BYPASSED THE CLEAN CONTRACT.
This read valid = np.arange(min(3, depth)) for any study with fewer than three real valid slots, and then handed that to _centres, which checked cleanliness AGAINST THE SYNTHETIC SET.

Slots 0,1,2 sit inside the first typed group, so centre 1 passed every test in _centres and the study served k windows built from BLANK slots -- measured on F's rendered rule with 44-slot masks holding zero, one and two valid entries: 12/12 windows touching blanks, with no diagnostic anywhere.
_centres's RuntimeError, written to refuse exactly this, could not fire, because by the time it ran the mask said the study was fine.
The validity set is now the REAL one.
A study that cannot be drawn cleanly is not pretended into one: training -- REFUSE.
An unlearnable bag of blank triplets is worse than a fold that stops, and a fold that stops gets looked at. serving -- fall back to the span rule and SAY SO.

The layout is one fixed (76, 3, res, res) uint8 block per study -- WINDOWS, already triplets, not slices -- plus a (76,) validity mask.

make_bag returns (N, 3, res, res) and the windows inside a slot are STRIDED across its span rather than stepping one slice at a time (measured: w0[1] != w1[0] for slots 1-4), so a triplet cannot be rebuilt from a compact slice volume and is stored whole.
That is why this corpus is 148 GB and not the 49.4 GB T121 budgeted for it.
A half-written corpus is the failure this refuses.

Built for the card we actually have.

The public trainer this replaces assumes a 24 GB card and offers no gradient accumulation, so on anything smaller the only lever is --bs, and dropping the batch is not a cheaper version of the recipe -- gradient noise, the effective learning rate under OneCycle and the normalisation statistics all move together.
Accumulation is the whole point of this file: --bs 2 --accum 4 puts the same 8 studies into every optimizer step as --bs 8 does, on 6 GiB instead of 16.
Measured envelope, RTX 4070 Laptop (7.62 GiB), bf16 + channels_last + gradient checkpointing, k = 12 (T111, 2026-09-17):
res 384 bs 2 7.13 GiB 45.7 ms/window 10.6 h for 16 epochs res 352 bs 2 6.06 GiB 38.1 ms/window 8.8 h for 16 epochs res 320 bs 2 5.66 GiB 30.9 ms/window 7.2 h for 16 epochs
For comparison a Kaggle T4 measured 207 ms/window.
Gradient checkpointing is not optional -- without it res 352 bs 1 runs out of memory asking for 24 MiB.

Because 8.8 h is longer than any fold this project has run, and the operator ruling of 2026-08-26 caps the local card at one fold before a cooldown, --resume is a requirement rather than a nicety: it restores the optimizer, the schedule, the epoch counter and all four RNG streams, and refuses to continue a checkpoint written under a different recipe.

fields that define the recipe: a checkpoint may only be resumed by a run that agrees with it on every one of them, because the schedule and the optimizer state are meaningless across a change to any bag_corpus joins RECIPE because it decides WHAT THE MODEL IS SHOWN.

A resume that silently changed corpora would keep an optimizer state fitted to one input distribution and continue on another -- the same class as the clean_windows mismatch T119 registered, one layer out.

Without this default, --resume on the fold that was training when it landed would refuse on a field that did not exist when the checkpoint was written -- a same-recipe check failing a run that IS the same recipe.

T120 finding 3: without the default, got.get("clean_windows") is None on every pre-T119 checkpoint, the comparison below is unconditional, and so --resume refused a legacy fold EVEN WITH --dirty-windows EXPLICITLY PASSED -- the one flag combination that describes exactly what those checkpoints are.
The mismatch printed as (None, False), which reads as a real disagreement rather than as a missing key.
Absent means False, and that is a fact about the world, not a convenience. Every checkpoint written before T119 was trained on the old span rule, so False is what those files mean.

The default therefore makes a legacy DIRTY resume succeed and a legacy CLEAN resume refuse -- which is correct in both directions: resuming a dirty fold under the clean rule would change the input distribution halfway through a fold and keep the optimizer state that was fitted to the other one.
Absent means the legacy slot corpus, which is what every checkpoint written before the dicom_bag path existed was trained on.
Deterministic: k_eval centres spread evenly, so a score is the model's.
Printed because it decides whether a checkpoint is scorable by the adopted notebook, which applies 'imagenet' to every arm.
A run's log must say which distribution its weights were fitted on.
THE T119 RULE HAS NOTHING TO DO HERE, and that is the point of the corpus rather than an omission.
Every stored window was rendered inside ONE typed slot from ONE series, so a triplet spanning two series is not merely filtered out -- it cannot be represented.
--dirty-windows has no meaning against a dicom_bag corpus: there are no boundary-crossing windows in it to keep.
Drop the flag, or train on --corpus if you are reproducing a pre-T121 fold.
persistent_workers IS OFF, and it is off on purpose.
It applies to BOTH corpora: BagWindows keys its draw on (seed, epoch, index) exactly as StudyWindows does, so a frozen worker freezes its augmentation too.
src/coat_data.py says the per-epoch window resampling IS the augmentation -- "the same study presents differently each time;
apart from a mild intensity jitter nothing else is augmented" -- and set_epoch writes self.epoch in the PARENT.
With persistent workers the workers are never re-forked, so their copy keeps the epoch it was forked with, and the workers fork at the first iter(tdl), AFTER set_epoch(0).
Every epoch then serves the identical tensor for a given study and only the shuffle order changes.

Measured on the real StudyWindows and the real corpus: frozen ep0/1/2 x.sum = 39484.996094, bit-identical correct ep1 44863.140625, ep2 40768.812500 The registered recipe passes --workers 4, so the arm was training on 12 of ~42 legal window centres per study for all 16 epochs -- a fixed augmented copy of the corpus rather than a resampled one.

src/dataset.py:285 states the rule for the OTHER trainer in as many words: "Keep persistent_workers off, or workers keep the epoch they were forked with and the mirror stops varying." This file was written later and set it on.
The cost of turning it off is a worker re-fork per epoch, which is seconds against a 3.5 h fold.

Evaluation sees k_eval windows per study, not k, so reusing --bs would put bsk_eval windows through the backbone in one forward -- at bs 2, k 12, k_eval 24 that is 48 against training's 24, and the allocator was observed to hit OOM and recover on a probe run.
Size the eval batch so a forward never exceeds the training forward.
THE SWA ACCUMULATOR IS INITIALISED BEFORE THE RESUME BLOCK, and that is the whole of this fix.

It used to live below it, so a resume reset it to empty -- and a fold interrupted anywhere inside its last --swa-epochs epochs then shipped a .swa.pt that was ONE epoch's weights, under a recipe still claiming swa_epochs 3, past the 0.85 floor, with exit 0.
Nothing downstream can tell: push_arm.py reads recipe and res, and neither records n_avg.
src/train.py -- which this trainer's docstring says it was lifted from -- persists both (train.py:887-888, :975).
--resume refuses a different recipe.
Mismatched: {bad}.
The optimizer state and the schedule position are only meaningful under the recipe that wrote them.
A checkpoint written before this fix carries no swa, which is not an error -- it is a fold that had not reached its tail, or one written by the old code.
Either way the honest value is "nothing accumulated yet", and the short-average refusal below is what catches the second case.

the guard is <, not +1 <, which would leave the schedule one step short of its floor and never reach the end of the cycle
ACCUMULATE, THEN SAVE.
THE ORDER IS THE FIX.
This ran the other way round: .last.pt was written and the current epoch was folded into the average afterwards.
So a checkpoint written at epoch N inside the tail carried the accumulator as it stood BEFORE N -- and a resume from it silently dropped one tail epoch.
On the 16-epoch / tail-3 recipe every fold actually runs, a crash after epoch 14's save resumes with n_avg=1, runs epoch 15, and ends with a 2-of-3 average.
That no longer ships (the gate below REFUSES 0 < n_avg < tail), so the defect is not silent any more -- but refusing is not the same as working.
The live cost was the whole fold: ~3.3 h of GPU that cannot produce a shippable checkpoint, from a resume the launch scripts perform AUTOMATICALLY whenever <stem>.last.pt exists.

With the order corrected, .last.pt at epoch N carries every tail epoch up to and including N, epoch: N still means "completed through N", and a resume at N+1 continues the average instead of restarting a short one.

Before the tail is entered the keys are still written -- {} and 0 -- because a resume must be able to tell "no epochs averaged yet" from "the accumulator was lost", and only an explicit key can say the first.
THE ARGMAX IS NOT WRITTEN UNDER --train-gold.
Selecting the shipped checkpoint by gold_auc > best when the model trained on those 58 studies picks the epoch that overfits them hardest -- actively harmful, not merely uninformative.
With gold held out the old behaviour stands.
T115/H10: this table is THIS epoch's, and best_gold_auc above is the maximum over all of them.
Pairing an argmax scalar with a last-epoch table under one roof is the T003 attribution defect;
the key now says which epoch it belongs to so the two cannot be read as one thing.

This is the join that decides whether a day of 4090 training becomes a leaderboard score or a wasted card.

CoatMIL and the notebook's RaptorClassifier are mathematically identical -- same LayerNorm, same Sequential(Linear(F,256), Tanh, Dropout, Linear(256,12)), same clsW/clsb, same einsum -- but ours nests the head as a submodule and theirs holds it as direct attributes, and their loader is strict=True.
Eight characters of key prefix stand between a trained arm and a scored one, and the failure would land at the END of an eight-hour Kaggle run.
The reference class is EXTRACTED FROM THE NOTEBOOK, never retyped.
A hand-copied reference drifts the moment either side changes and the test keeps passing -- which is this project's logged defect class, a check that passes for the wrong reason.
If their class changes, the extraction changes with it and this test fails, which is the only reason to have it.
